text:
Jordan P.: Need help removing my ex from my medical after divorce decree finalized last week. Filed on 2025-03-10 but decree date listed as 2025-02-28. Carrier says QLE window expired. What do we submit?

Asha (People Ops): Sorry you're dealing with this. Short version: carriers usually accept the divorce decree as the QLE proof if it shows final judgment date. The QLE date is typically the date of divorce (judgment date). If your filing date is later, we can still submit the decree plus a cover letter explaining the judgment date.

Jordan P.: Carrier rep claims only filings within 30 days count and is rejecting because our HR portal says "filed 3/10." Can Redwood file an exception with carrier?

Max (Benefits Ops): We can escalate. Please upload the signed divorce decree (redact kids' SSNs), and the court docket page showing the judgment date. Also helpful: proof of name change if any, and separation agreement if it lists the judgment date. We'll bundle and ask carrier to accept retroactive removal effective the judgment date.

Jordan P.: Uploaded: "jordan_divorce_decree_1857777777.pdf" and "court_docket_1857777782.png"

Benefits Bot: Upload received from Jordan P. File IDs: ux_1857777783, ux_1857777784. Status: queued for review.

Asha (People Ops): Got the uploads. Max, I'll DM you the secure link. Note: redact SSNs — we can accept last 4. Jordan, thanks for redacting.

Max (Benefits Ops): Reviewing now. Quick FYI on outcomes: 1) Carrier approves retro to judgment date -> we'll remove spouse and refund premium difference (processed as payroll adjustment/retro pay). 2) Carrier denies -> spouse stays covered until next open enrollment or until COBRA election is processed; ex will be offered COBRA per carrier rules.

Lina (Payroll): For refunds if retroactive, we process a net payroll adjustment in the following pay run and will notify you of tax treatment. If spouse had claims, carriers may have different claim adjudication rules; we won't reduce any claims already paid by plan.

Jordan P.: If carrier denies, how long does spouse get COBRA? Also do I need to notify ex?

Asha (People Ops): COBRA timeline: typically 60-day election window from the date of qualifying event notice (which is usually the date coverage ends). Carrier provides election packet. For notification: company sends required COBRA/general notice to former spouse per federal/state rules; don't contact them directly for the official notice. We'll handle required employer notices.

Max (Benefits Ops): I filed an initial exception request to the carrier with the decree and docket at 1857777815. Carrier acknowledged receipt and gave an initial SLA of 7-10 business days for decision.

Legal Ops Bot: Reminder: do not share full SSNs or bank account details in thread. Use secure uploads.

Jordan P.: Got it. Anything I should expect from payroll in the meantime?

Lina (Payroll): Nothing until benefits confirms effective date. If approved retro, we'll calculate premium refund and adjust the subsequent payroll. If coverage continues and your ex elects COBRA, payroll won't change unless they elected employer-subsidized coverage in rare cases. We'll post an estimate in DM if you want one.

Max (Benefits Ops): Carrier requested one more doc: a copy of the marriage certificate showing original marriage date. They say they want to validate the marriage timeline. Jordan, can you upload a redacted marriage cert?

Jordan P.: Uploaded marriage_cert_redacted.pdf (1857777832)

Benefits Bot: Upload received File ID ux_1857777833 Status: under review.

Asha (People Ops): Thanks. Max, I'll follow-up with carrier case #C-185777 and escalate if needed. Jordan, I'll update the thread when we have a decision. Meanwhile, avoid sending any PHI in the channel.

Jordan P.: Appreciate it. One last q: if retro removal approved, will claims paid out for spouse be clawed back?

Max (Benefits Ops): No. Claims already paid by the plan stay paid. Retro removal affects enrollment and premium adjustments only; carriers rarely try to re-open paid claims for situations like this.

Lina (Payroll): I'll prepare an estimated payroll delta once Max confirms effective date. Ping me in DM if you want a breakdown after approval.

Asha (People Ops): Following up: carrier responded at 1857777888 - they're reviewing, expect final by 10 business days. Will update. :thumbsup:
